faq.question: What is the best seafood restaurant in Kota Kinabalu?
faq.answer: Welcome Seafood is the most famous (7,300+ reviews). KK Garden has the highest rating (4.5★). Locals prefer Suang Tain or New Luyang. Gayang and Kampung Nelayan are top halal options.

faq.question: How much does seafood cost in Kota Kinabalu?
faq.answer: Budget options like Fatt Kee start at MYR 15/person ($3.50). Mid-range averages MYR 30–60 ($7–14). Premium meals run MYR 60–100 ($14–23). Dinner for two with crab, prawns, and fish costs MYR 100–150 ($23–35).

faq.question: Are there halal seafood restaurants in Kota Kinabalu?
faq.answer: Yes. Kampung Nelayan and Gayang Seafood are halal certified. Most others are Muslim-friendly including Welcome Seafood, Fatt Kee, Fish Market, and Suang Tain.

faq.question: What seafood dishes should I try in Kota Kinabalu?
faq.answer: Must-try: butter prawns, kam heong crab, steamed fish with soy sauce, salted egg prawns. Local specialties: hinava (raw fish salad) and latok (sea grapes). Sichuan mala crab at Jumbo Palace is a standout.

faq.question: When is the best time to eat seafood in Kota Kinabalu?
faq.answer: March–October has the freshest catches. Dinner (6–9 PM) is liveliest. Some restaurants only open afternoon. Fatt Kee opens at 7 AM.

faq.question: Where do locals eat seafood in Kota Kinabalu?
faq.answer: Locals prefer Suang Tain, New Luyang, Fatt Kee, and Gayang over tourist spots. KK Central Market is popular for wholesale fresh seafood.
